task.task_description: You're a production planner at a packaged food factory, and you need to put together next week's schedule for several packaging lines. You have customer orders, demand forecasts, inventory levels, equipment availability, staff schedules, and planned maintenance times to work with. Products take different amounts of time to run and need different packaging setups. Switching products can also mean stopping to clean and reset the equipment. Your task is to build a schedule the factory can actually deliver, taking into account deadlines, line capacity, available materials, staffing, and production priorities. If there isn't enough capacity or some materials won't be available, work through the options with production management before sending the schedule to the factory floor.

operational_subtasks.description: Gather and review the relevant customer orders, forecasts, inventory, equipment availability, staff schedules, and planned maintenance information.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumes the listed planning records are available through routine systems and need a single review for the upcoming week; this estimate covers accessing and consolidating information, not analyzing production requirements.

operational_subtasks.description: Translate orders and forecasts into product quantities and establish the required deadlines and production priorities.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumes a representative weekly plan with several products and that order and forecast information from SUB001 is readily available. The estimate covers reconciling demand and determining what needs to be produced, without re-gathering source records.

operational_subtasks.description: Compare required production quantities with available inventory and identify material shortfalls or timing constraints.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumes one comparison of required quantities against the available inventory information, with additional attention only to material constraints identified. This uses the requirements from SUB002 and inventory already reviewed in SUB001.

operational_subtasks.description: Determine feasible product-to-line assignments using production rates, packaging setup and cleaning/reset needs, equipment availability, staffing, and maintenance times.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumes several packaging lines and products with differing run and changeover needs; the estimate covers matching those known requirements to available line, staff, and time information. It does not include building or validating the full schedule.

operational_subtasks.description: Assign production quantities to lines and time periods, sequencing runs to account for priorities, deadlines, capacity, materials, staffing, and planned downtime.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumes a routine multi-line weekly plan and that the demand, material, and line assessments are available from earlier work. The estimate covers constructing and adjusting a workable draft, not a separate full review of the inputs.

operational_subtasks.description: Check the draft for conflicts or unmet requirements involving line capacity, deadlines, materials, staffing, equipment availability, and maintenance.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: One incremental feasibility check is expected for each weekly schedule; this uses the draft and prior findings rather than repeating their analysis. The estimate allows time to identify and characterize any constraints for resolution.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Discuss constraint options with production management
operational_subtasks.description: When capacity or material constraints remain, discuss practical production options with production management and determine the agreed adjustments.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumes this discussion is needed for approximately 0.3 of weekly schedules; this is a planning assumption, not a supplied operating rate. The per-occurrence estimate covers preparing for and discussing the identified options, using findings from SUB006.

operational_subtasks.description: Update the draft schedule to reflect adjustments agreed with production management.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumes revision is needed when the conditional management discussion occurs, for approximately 0.3 occurrences per weekly schedule. The estimate covers incremental schedule changes using the existing draft and agreed decisions, not rebuilding the plan from scratch.

operational_subtasks.description: Prepare and send the final schedule, including line assignments and timing, to the factory-floor recipients who will use it.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: One distribution is expected per weekly schedule. The estimate covers preparing the usable schedule communication and sending it through the established channel, without including production execution or follow-up.

parent_output_contract.output_unit: One weekly production schedule for the factory's packaging lines
parent_output_contract.completion_boundary: The schedule has been checked against the stated planning constraints, any required options have been discussed with production management and incorporated, and the final schedule has been sent to the factory floor.
scope_exclusions: Executing production or monitoring schedule adherence
Procuring materials or carrying out other management actions agreed during constraint discussions
Changing customer orders or revising the schedule after it has been issued
